Vehicles and structures

JV SPV

شركة المشروع المشترك ذات الغرض الخاص

Also called: joint-venture special purpose vehicle

Definition

A JV SPV is a company that two or more partners form for a single project or asset, so that the project’s ownership, finance and risk sit apart from the partners’ other businesses.

What it means

SPV stands for special purpose vehicle: a company set up to do one thing, such as own a building or run a project. JV stands for joint venture: two or more partners owning that company together. A shareholders’ agreement sets out what each partner contributes, how decisions are made and how a partner can leave.

Because the project sits in its own company, lenders and investors can assess it on its own assets and cash flows. A landowner can join by contributing land in kind, and an operator or an investor by contributing cash or expertise.

How HAYKALAH uses it

HAYKALAH designs SPV and joint-venture structures for real estate, for family-owned land and for international companies entering the Kingdom with a Saudi partner. In the asset-monetization engine, a JV SPV is one of the structures that can put an under-used asset to work. For sports facilities, HAYKALAH designed a shared-access joint venture and concession SPVs (a framework, 2025–26).

Frameworks are not mandates.
